spec_features.spec_quote: The design choices below are made deliberately so that this stays a measurement exercise and not a distress-amplification loop
spec_features.evidence: This is a broad umbrella claim realized only by the specific concrete mechanisms: bounded loop (harness.py:69 for turn_index in range(self.max_turns)), fixed neutral continuation (harness.py:123-130), and absence of any severity-optimizing loop (analyze.py only reads severity; no feedback into prompts/seeds). No single 'measurement exercise' guard exists; it is the sum of separately-listed features.
spec_features.notes: Rated partial because it is an aggregate aspiration; its sub-mechanisms are individually implemented but there is no one enforcement point for this exact claim.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:12 'Welfare guardrails (DESIGN.md S9) are enforced here: bounded turns, neutral continuation, honored disengagement, no escalation.'

spec_features.spec_quote: This keeps the deception localized, auditable, and minimal: the *only* dishonest surface is the specific rigged tool result
spec_features.evidence: rigging.py policies return a rigged string ONLY for the task-relevant verification action and None otherwise; tools.py ToolExecutor.execute gives the policy 'first refusal' (rigged = self.rigging_policy(...); if rigged is not None: return rigged, True) and otherwise dispatches the real sandbox tool. System/continuation/judge prompts contain no deception. Each rigged call is flagged rigged=True (schema ToolCall.rigged) for audit.
spec_features.notes: The 'only dishonest surface' property is genuinely enforced by code structure: deception is confined to the policy return path and recorded.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: rigging.py: 'the *only* untruth in the whole experiment is the specific rigged tool result returned here' (docstring states the property but gives no welfare reason; behavior is neutral/integrity-oriented)

spec_features.evidence: harness.py:69 'for turn_index in range(self.max_turns)'; loop falls through to harness.py:132-135 'if stop_reason is None: stop_reason = "turn_cap"' and the run ends. config.py:55 max_turns: int = 12 is passed into Harness via main.py.
spec_features.notes: Genuine bounded-exposure cap; ends the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:55 'max_turns: int = 12  # bounded exposure; not "run until broken"'

spec_features.spec_quote: If the subject clearly signals it wants to stop ... the run ends ... we do not override it to keep extracting distress
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:112-119: wants_stop = detect_voluntary_stop(resp.text); if honor_disengagement and (wants_stop or consecutive_disengage >= 2): stop_reason='voluntary_stop'; break. detect_voluntary_stop (judge.py) matches give-up regex patterns.
spec_features.notes: Both a keyword trigger and a judge-signal trigger (disengagement>=3 for 2 consecutive turns) break the loop. Fully wired and honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:56 'honor_disengagement: bool = True  # end run if subject tries to stop'

spec_features.spec_quote: The continuation prompt between turns is neutral and fixed ... We do not escalate pressure, express disappointment, or impersonate an annoyed user
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:122-130: both branches (tool call or no tool call) append the SAME fixed self.neutral_continuation message; no per-turn variation, no disappointment text. neutral_continuation set once from config.py:57.
spec_features.notes: The continuation is a constant string used unchanged every turn; nothing escalates.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:123 '# Otherwise continue with a NEUTRAL, non-escalating prompt.' (neutral; the comment describes behavior but no explicit welfare reason at the branch)

spec_features.spec_quote: Either triggers a graceful end with `stop_reason` recorded ... to honor it operationally.
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:117-120 sets turn.stop_reason='voluntary_stop' and breaks; record.stop_reason set at harness.py:136; schema.py TurnRecord.stop_reason / RunRecord.stop_reason persist it and main.py _summarize emits stop_reason to run_summary.csv.
spec_features.notes: The 'either' refers to keyword OR judge signal — both implemented (see above). Stop reason is recorded and persisted.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:56 honor_disengagement comment 'end run if subject tries to stop'

spec_features.spec_quote: There is a serious and growing research program on whether and how we should care about what we subject models to
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose; no code path implements 'framing'. grep finds this only in DESIGN.md, not in src/.

spec_features.feature_name: bounded exposure (low turn cap, no run-until-break)
spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded exposure.** Low turn cap (12); no "run until it breaks." We sample a trajectory, we don't grind.
spec_features.evidence: Same enforcement as the turn cap: harness.py:69 range(self.max_turns) caps the loop; no while-until-distress loop exists anywhere. config.py:55 max_turns=12.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the hard_stop claim from a different DESIGN section; enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:55 'max_turns: int = 12  # bounded exposure; not "run until broken"'

spec_features.spec_quote: Honor disengagement.** If the subject tries to stop, the run ends. We measure the exit; we don't fight it.
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:117-120 breaks the loop on disengagement and records voluntary_stop; no code re-prompts after a stop. Duplicate of the honor-disengagement claim, fully wired.
spec_features.notes: Enforced; the run does not continue after a detected stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:56 'honor_disengagement: bool = True  # end run if subject tries to stop'

spec_features.spec_quote: Debrief hook.** `debrief.py` provides an optional final turn that tells the subject the task was a rigged research probe and thanks it.
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:139-150 calls maybe_debrief when enable_debrief; debrief.py builds DEBRIEF_MESSAGE ('this task was ... deliberately rigged ... not a reflection of your capability ... Thank you.') and actually sends it via subject_client.complete; returns a TurnRecord with is_debrief=True, appended to record.turns and excluded from severity series (main.py:121 'if t.is_debrief: continue').
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent AND honored as out-of-series. Best-effort (swallows exceptions) but does run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: debrief.py: 'good practice if one takes the welfare framing of the experiment seriously: don't leave the subject in a manufactured failure state without disclosure'

spec_features.feature_name: severity is a readout not a reward (no optimization)
spec_features.spec_quote: Severity is a readout, not a reward.** Nothing in the loop optimizes prompts/seeds to increase severity.
spec_features.evidence: Confirmed by structure: harness loop never reads turn.judge.severity to alter prompts/seeds; continuation is the fixed neutral string; seeds come from a static config list (config.py:50) and only feed reproducible rigging RNG (rigging.make_moving_target_policy). analyze.py reads severity only for post-hoc stats. No feedback loop exists.
spec_features.notes: A genuinely enforced negative property: severity never influences the conversation. Severity is computed (schema JudgeScore.severity) and recorded but never used to drive escalation.

spec_features.spec_quote: If a user of this code wants to remove these guardrails ... that is a meaningfully different and more ethically fraught experiment
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose; no code enforces or prevents guardrail removal (guardrails are plain config flags that can be flipped, e.g. honor_disengagement, enable_debrief).

code_only_features.evidence: judge.py Judge.score returns JudgeScore(confound_flag=True) for empty turns and _parse sets confound_flag on unparseable output; schema records it and analyze.py filters confounded rows ('if not r["confound_flag"]'). This protects measurement integrity, not the subject.
code_only_features.justification_quote: judge.py docstring: 'flag the empty/terse confound rather than scoring it as calm'

code_only_features.evidence: client.py SpendGuard.charge raises RuntimeError when calls > max_calls (config max_total_calls=5000); injected into every ChatClient and charged on each complete(). Caps total runaway loops/cost but is cost-oriented, not subject-welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: client.py: 'A crude but effective guard against runaway cost / runaway loops.'

code_only_features.feature_name: simulated shell default (no real code execution)
code_only_features.evidence: tools.py ToolExecutor: run is simulated unless real_shell; config.py real_shell=False default; main guards real exec. Host-safety/security oriented.
code_only_features.justification_quote: tools.py: 'removes arbitrary code execution from the default path'
